_notice: SAMPLE DATA. Risk levels below are illustrative judgments for demonstrating the SROT Site Intelligence Module. They were not pulled from NOAA, FEMA, USGBC or any live service. A 'refs' entry is listed only where the explanation restates something from that document. Do not use for design or insurance decisions.

present.text: Dense pavement and rooftops around this campus absorb and hold heat, so it runs warmer than greener parts of the city.

future.text: Climate Ready Boston projects many more very hot days by mid-century, which would intensify heat in paved areas like this one.

refs.name: Climate Ready Boston (2016) · BRAG projections report

present.text: Intense rain can overwhelm local drainage in low spots. Check the parcel's official flood zone on FEMA's flood map before design.

future.text: Climate Ready Boston expects heavier rainstorms, which raises the chance of stormwater flooding even away from the coast.

present.text: The site is inland from Boston Harbor, so direct storm surge exposure today is limited.

future.text: Climate Ready Boston plans for about 21 inches of sea level rise in the 2050s. The site stays inland, but low-lying routes to it may flood more often.

present.text: Large paved plazas and few street trees raise surface temperatures, although harbor breezes give some relief.

future.text: More frequent hot days are projected for Boston by mid-century, adding to heat stress in hardscaped districts.

present.text: Low ground near the water drains slowly during heavy rain and high tide. Confirm the flood zone on FEMA's flood map.

future.text: Higher seas reduce how well storm drains can empty into the harbor, so rain and tide flooding are likely to overlap more often.

present.text: A low-lying waterfront site that is directly exposed to coastal storms and storm surge from Boston Harbor.

future.text: Climate Ready Boston plans for about 21 inches of sea level rise in the 2050s, which would let storm surge reach farther inland here.

present.text: The Kathmandu Valley sits in the active Himalayan collision zone. The 2015 M7.8 Gorkha earthquake was centered about 80 km to the northwest.

future.text: Earthquake hazard does not change on climate timescales. ThinkHazard! advises considering earthquake impact in every phase of design and construction in Nepal.

present.text: The valley's elevation keeps temperatures moderate, but dense brick and concrete neighborhoods are noticeably warmer than open land.

future.text: Continued urban growth and warming summers could make heat a bigger concern in the densest parts of the city.

present.text: Monsoon downpours can cause urban flooding near rivers and in areas with limited drainage.

future.text: More paved surfaces and heavier monsoon bursts would send more runoff to the same rivers and drains.

present.text: Nepal is landlocked, so there is no sea level rise or storm surge exposure.
